subject: Nanotechnology
title: Metamaterials: Engineering Light
description: A quick, practical guide to Metamaterials: Engineering Light.

hook.text: No natural material bends light backward — but metamaterials with nano-structured unit cells can.

buildup.text: Metamaterials are arrays of sub-wavelength elements that produce optical properties not found in nature.

discovery.text: Negative refractive index materials bend light the opposite way — enabling flat lenses and cloaking concepts.

twist.text: Most metamaterials only work at specific frequencies — broadband negative refraction remains elusive.

climax.text: Metasurfaces — single-layer metamaterials — are practical enough for flat lenses already in smartphone cameras.

punchline.text: Arrange atoms into patterns and you invent optical properties.

quiz.question: What makes metamaterials different from natural materials?
options: They are made from heavier elements
Their sub-wavelength structures produce optical properties not found in any natural material
They only work with ultraviolet light
